title: Exercise 7A · Q9(c)
summary: Find AB² in ΔABC, then use it directly in ΔABD to get AD.
alt: Exercise 7A · Q9(c): In the figure, AC = 19 cm, BD = 8 cm, DC = 6 cm and ∠B = 90°. Find the value of c, the length of AD.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: In the figure, **AC = 19 cm**, **BD = 8 cm**, **DC = 6 cm** and **∠B = 90°**. We have to find **c**, the length of **AD**.

steps.title: Find BC
steps.narration: To use ΔABC we need **BC**.\[\begin{aligned}BC &= BD + DC \\ &= 8 + 6 = 14\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔABC, **∠B = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **AC**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. We only need **AB²** for the next triangle, so we stop before taking the square root. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ \role{legA}{AB^2} &= \role{hyp}{AC^2} - \role{legB}{BC^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ \role{legA}{AB^2} &= \role{hyp}{AC^2} - \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{19^2} - \role{legB}{14^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{361} - \role{legB}{196} \\ &= \role{legA}{165}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔABD, **∠B = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **AD**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. Here **AB² = 165** from the last step. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AD^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BD^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and add
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and add.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AD^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BD^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{165} + \role{legB}{8^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{165} + \role{legB}{64} \\ &= \role{hyp}{229}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 229 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AD^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BD^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{165} + \role{legB}{8^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{165} + \role{legB}{64} \\ &= \role{hyp}{229} \\ \role{hyp}{AD} &= \sqrt{229} = \role{ans}{15.1\ \text{cm}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Do we need AB?

options.label: Yes — we must find AB first
No — AB is not needed at all

challenges.prompt: To find AD² we use AD² = AB² + BD². Do we need the value of **AB** itself?
challenges.hint: Look at which quantity appears in the equation.
challenges.explain: The equation uses AB², which we already have (165). Taking the square root and squaring again would just waste time.

takeaways: Sometimes you need only a **square**, not the side itself — keep it as it is and use it in the next triangle.
Pythagoras' theorem works only in **right-angled** triangles — mark every right angle in the figure first.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
